title: Maryland PSC Order No. 92521 (Case No. 9866)
text:
ORDER NO. 92521 

Review of Next Generation Energy Act 
Transmission-Connected Energy Storage 
Proposals – Round 1 

_________________________________ 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 
BEFORE THE 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
OF MARYLAND 
__________ 
Case No. 9866 
__________ 

Issue Date: July 10, 2026 

ORDER GRANTING INTERVENTION OUT-OF-TIME 
I. 
BACKGROUND 
During the 2025 Session of the Maryland General Assembly, the legislature passed the 
Next Generation Energy Act (“NGEA”),1 which required, inter alia, that the Commission issue at 
least two solicitations for a cumulative 1,600 MWs of front-of-the-meter transmission-connected 
energy storage, with each energy storage device having a minimum 4-hour duration. The 
Commission issued the first round NGEA Energy Storage Request for Applications (“RFA”) on 
December 24, 2025.2 On March 2, 2026, the Commission received five transmission-connected 
energy storage applications in response to the RFA. The Commission subsequently initiated the 
instant Case No. 9866 to evaluate all applications deemed administratively complete and to 
conduct evidentiary hearings to determine which projects will receive Energy Storage Capacity 
Credits under the NGEA.3 

1 See PUA §§ 7-1224-1229, as enrolled in Senate Bill 937/ House Bill 1035. 
2 Maillog No. 325670, Notice of NGEA Energy Storage Request for Applications - Round 1 (Dec. 24, 2025). 
3 Maillog No. 327891, Notice Initiating Proceeding, Establishing Workgroup, and Extending Confidential Treatment 
for Next Generation Energy Act Applications (Mar. 13, 2026). 

2 

On May 1, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Pre-Hearing Conference,4 which 
established a deadline for seeking intervention on May 11, 2026. The Commission held a pre-
hearing conference on May 13, 2026, during which it adopted a procedural schedule and granted 
all pending petitions to intervene (“Procedural Schedule”).5 
Following the pre-hearing conference, Delegate Lauren Arikan filed a Petition to Intervene, 
out-of-time, on May 14, 2026.6 The next day, Harford County Executive Robert G. Cassilly (the 
“County”) filed a Petition to Intervene on behalf of Harford County residents (referred together 
with Delegate Arikan as the “Petitioners”).7 
II. 
PETITIONS TO INTERVENE 
In her Petition, Delegate Arikan highlighted strong community opposition and 
apprehension regarding the proposed energy storage projects and their potential impacts on 
residential neighborhoods, agricultural land, environmental resources, public infrastructure, and 
public safety. She also raised concerns over emergency response preparedness and the overall 
adequacy of transparency and public engagement throughout the process. She asserted the 
decisions made in this matter could directly and adversely affect the interests of Harford County 
residents.8 
The County’s Petition also expressed serious environmental and public safety concerns 
regarding a proposed 500 MW transmission-connected energy storage facility, highlighting that

3 

the proposed site for the facility is bisected by a tributary that directly feeds into Deer Creek—a 
critical drinking water source for Harford County, Baltimore County, the City of Aberdeen, and 
Baltimore City. The County received substantial public feedback expressing concerns over 
drinking water protection, local emergency response capacity, environmental impacts, and a 
distinct lack of transparency and public engagement surrounding the proposed project.9 
III. 
COMMISSION DECISION 
In determining whether to grant a petition to intervene out-of-time, the Commission 
considers several factors, including the purpose for which intervention is sought, the probability 
of prejudice to the parties already in the case, the extent to which the proceedings have progressed, 
and the reason or reasons for the delay in seeking intervention.10 Here, the Commission weighed 
the following factors in favor of granting intervention out-of-time: (1) both Petitioners filed shortly 
after the intervention deadline had passed; (2) Delegate Arikan and Harford County each claimed 
interests and raised concerns that are not adequately represented by other parties to this proceeding; 
(3) none of the other parties opposed the Petitions; and (4) admitting both Petitioners at this stage 
of the proceeding—prior to the submission of the other parties’ direct testimony and before the 
evidentiary hearing—would cause little to no prejudice to the other parties. Furthermore, the 
Commission finds no purposeful intent by either Petitioner to delay seeking intervention. Delegate 
Arikan’s Petition, although filed on May 14, 2026, was dated May 11, 2026. The County filed its 
Petition immediately upon learning that Power Advisory LLC had submitted its administrative 
completeness report to the Commission. 

9 Harford Cnty Petition at 1. 
10 See generally, Maryland-Nat’l Cap. Park & Plan. Comm’n v. Town of Wash. Grove, 408 Md. 37, 70 (2009). 

4 

To strike an appropriate balance between safeguarding against prejudice to the other parties 
while also ensuring the Petitioners’ prompt participation in this proceeding, the Commission will 
not adjust the procedural schedule. However, the Petitioners shall have the opportunity to engage 
in discovery and/or submit written testimony, if they so choose. To facilitate their entry, the 
Commission makes the following accommodations: 
(1) 
Petitioners may propound discovery on other Parties. To the extent 
Petitioners propound discovery requests, the respondent(s) shall use best 
efforts to accelerate their discovery responses within three business days of 
service. Any objections to the Petitioners’ discovery requests made during 
this time must be served within 1 business day. Unless specified otherwise 
herein, any discovery propounded by the Petitioners shall be in accordance 
with the Commission’s May 14, 2026 Procedural Schedule;11 and 
(2) 
Petitioners shall have additional time to file any direct testimony, which 
shall be due on July 22, 2026. However, Petitioners shall file any rebuttal 
testimony in accordance with the Commission’s Procedural Schedule. 
For the foregoing reasons, the Commission hereby grants the uncontested requests to 
intervene filed by Delegate Arikan (on her own behalf) and the Harford County Government, 
subject to the accommodations described in this Order.
